tone_patterns: Uses formal, institutional language with an emphasis on prudence, reliability, and governance-led decision-making.
Balances opportunity framing (value creation, resilience) with risk framing (mitigation, avoiding adverse impacts).
Employs forward-looking phrasing to describe expected future influence on financial planning across time horizons.
Maintains an explanatory tone that links sustainability actions to financial statement impacts without over-claiming.
paragraph_patterns: Opens with a short contextual statement that positions sustainability as integrated into strategic decision-making, followed by a parenthetical cross-reference to another section.
Uses subtopic-led paragraphs with a bold/label-like lead-in (e.g., a concept name) followed by narrative explanation.
Presents a ‘trade-offs’ narrative structure: identifies decision bodies, references guiding frameworks/policies, then explains balancing benefits vs returns and consideration of negative impacts.
Includes a ‘disclosure approach’ paragraph that explains the current period’s reporting posture (qualitative vs quantitative) and justifies it using reliability/materiality language.
Transitions from current-period description to forward-looking expectations, then to implications for portfolio/financial resilience.
Ends with a short commitment/next-steps paragraph indicating planned enhancements to quantitative reporting and/or resilience analysis in a future period.
heading_patterns: Numbered subsection headings (e.g., 3.x) used to segment the Strategy chapter into discrete IFRS-aligned themes.
Headings combine a short label with a descriptive phrase (e.g., linking strategy to decision-making or financial impacts).
Uses parallel heading structure for sequential topics (e.g., decision-making, financial impacts, resilience, approach).
Places the section title (e.g., Strategy) as a running header/footer element on each page in addition to subsection headings.
table_patterns: Uses a multi-column mapping table to connect material topics to financial statement line items and note references.
Table columns follow a hierarchy: Topic → Metric/Area → Statement location (Assets/Liabilities/Income Statement/Expenses) → Specific line items → References.
Employs grouped rows with category labels (e.g., Assets, Liabilities) and indented bullet sub-items beneath each category.
Uses concise bullet lists inside cells rather than long sentences.
Includes a dedicated ‘References’ column pointing to note numbers/sections to support traceability to audited financial statements.
Table is positioned after narrative that states sustainability impacts are reflected in financial statements, functioning as evidence linkage.
figure_or_diagram_patterns: Introduces figures with a numbered caption (e.g., Figure X) followed by a source link.
Uses external authoritative sources for scenario/analytical figures and cites the URL directly.
Figure reference appears near the related subsection (e.g., resilience or climate approach) rather than earlier general narrative.
pdf_layout_patterns: Page header/footer includes section name and report title; page number appears consistently at the bottom.
Two-column-like behavior appears in places: narrative blocks with controlled line lengths and frequent manual line breaks to fit layout constraints.
Subsection headings are visually separated from body text with whitespace, supporting scanability.
Tables span the page width and use clear grid alignment; bullets are used within cells to reduce text density.
Cross-references to other sections are embedded inline (parenthetical) rather than as footnotes.
Figure citation is placed as a short line item near the end of the page, separated from the main paragraph flow.
disclosure_language_patterns: Explicitly states how sustainability-related risks/opportunities may affect cash flows, access to finance, and cost of capital across short/medium/long term horizons.
Uses cautious qualifiers when discussing impacts (e.g., focusing on qualitative disclosures in the current period) and provides rationale tied to reliability/meaningfulness.
Connects sustainability activities to financial position, performance, and cash flows using accounting-style terminology.
Includes commitments framed as future reporting intentions (e.g., plans to quantify impacts in a later period) without asserting current quantified outcomes.
Uses ‘refer to’ language to direct readers to governance sections and financial statement notes for corroboration.
evidence_presentation_patterns: Triangulates narrative claims with (1) named internal frameworks/policies, (2) financial statement linkage via note references, and (3) external scenario/source references.
Uses a traceability approach: narrative assertion → table mapping to financial statement areas → note references.
Separates ‘current period’ evidence from ‘anticipated’ impacts, signaling different evidence strength levels.
Employs concrete accounting anchors (financial statements, notes) as the primary evidence mechanism rather than standalone sustainability metrics.
section_specific_observations: Strategy section blends governance integration, risk management, and financial impact discussion in a single flow, then branches into resilience and climate approach subsections.

The excerpt uses a deliberate progression: integration statement → decision-making trade-offs → ESG risk context → financial impact linkage → forward-looking outlook → resilience/approach signposting.
The section uses both narrative and structured artifacts (table, figure citation) to satisfy decision-useful disclosure expectations.
things_to_avoid_copying: Any company name or group references.
Any specific frameworks/policies by proprietary title; replace with generic equivalents (e.g., ‘sustainable finance framework’, ‘responsible investment policy’).
Any sector examples, product names, or instrument types that could identify the reference entity’s activities.
Any numeric amounts, dates, issuance volumes, currency figures, or time-bound commitments as written.
Any geographic references or region-specific positioning statements.
Any direct URLs presented in the reference; use a generic ‘source link’ pattern instead.
content_specific_items_detected_and_excl: Entity name and report title references.
Specific financing instrument types and labels.
Specific issuance amounts and currency values.
Specific note numbers and line-item labels as written (retained only as an abstract ‘note reference’ pattern).
Specific sector examples used to illustrate investment focus or high-risk sectors.
Specific future year mentioned for planned quantitative reporting.
Specific external source URL for scenario portal.
